Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — options for next year

Thanks Marissa — quick note from our side before the partner call. We like the idea of simplifying the term but want a path that lets us scale over Q1/Q2 without committing to full-year step-ups up front. Two asks: 1) a monthly ‘pay-as-you-grow’ overlay so we can add capacity mid-term without renegotiating the whole PO, and 2) an option to auto-renew at a reduced escalation if usage stays within the agreed band.

Can you share a concrete structure (ramp schedule + billing cadence) and an amendment draft we can show procurement? Also want an example invoice profile for a ramp from 20% to 80% over six months.

— Sophie

Hi Sophie — thanks, that’s helpful. I pushed a short playbook and a draft amendment to this thread (attached). High level proposal:

- Base term: 24 months co-term starting 2027-01-01 with a two-quarter flexible overlay.
- Pay-as-you-grow overlay: capacity can be increased monthly in 10% increments; overage invoiced monthly at a committed-discount rate with true-up at quarter-end.
- Rolling tilt: if Brightlane elects auto-renew, escalation for year-to-year auto-renew is capped at +3% unless usage grows beyond the top band (then triggers a tiered uplift).
- Safety net: ability to request one mid-term downsize (60-day notice) to avoid lock-in if usage contracts.

I attached: Redwood_Amendment_v3.pdf (draft showing clauses) and Capacity_Onboarding_SOW.xlsx (example ramp + invoice profile). Can Karthik weigh in on pricing tiers (cc’d) and Jonas/Legal if we need tighter language on auto-renew opt-out?

Next steps: if this is directionally acceptable, Sophie — can procurement confirm the required PO cadence (monthly vs quarterly)? If monthly, we’ll prepare doc for signing and propose a pilot month with burst credits.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec, Renewals | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Amendment_v3.pdf, Capacity_Onboarding_SOW.xlsx

Marissa — quick internal note after reading Sophie’s asks and the draft. Points for ops/legal/billing: 

1) Pricing bands: propose three overlay bands (0–30%, 31–60%, 61–100%) priced at 70%, 60%, and 50% of list respectively (i.e., deeper discount for larger adds). That keeps unit economics intact and gives a predictable invoice profile.
2) Billing cadence: monthly invoicing is fine but require a quarterly true-up and a minimum monthly invoice floor equal to 10% of committed spend to cover platform reservations.
3) Auto-renew language: we can implement a capped escalation (3%) but need an explicit clause for manual opt-out window (30 days prior to renewal) to satisfy procurement.
4) Risk: permitting too many mid-term increases without reservation capacity may cause scheduling contention in Dedicated pools. Suggest adding a 14-day capacity lead time for any >40% monthly increment.

Jonas — can you draft the 14-day/lead-time sentence and confirm SLA impact? Lauren — billing needs the sample invoice rows (I flagged a sample sheet).

-Karthik

Thanks — wording suggestion to include in the amendment: 

"Capacity Additions: Customer may request capacity increases in whole-percent increments not to exceed 40% of the then-current committed capacity in any single calendar month without prior written confirmation from Redwood. Requests exceeding 40% will be treated as expedited capacity changes and require 14 calendar days' notice; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to grant expedited changes subject to Dedicated pool availability and may apply temporary burst pricing."

SLA impact: expedited adds may incur a temporary best-effort latency degradation window (typically <72 hours) while capacity is rebalanced. We should surface this to the customer.

-Jonas

Sophie/Tom — appreciate the quick turnaround. We incorporated the feedback and attached a redline of the amendment (see Redwood_Amendment_v3.pdf). Highlights:

- Monthly pay-as-you-grow overlay with 10% minimum monthly invoice floor.
- Three-tier add bands with pricing tiers and quarterly true-up.
